claims.claim: In January 2019, SoftBank invested in WeWork at an implied valuation of $47 billion.
In 2018, WeWork generated $1.82 billion in revenue and suffered a net loss of $1.93 billion ($1.61B operating loss), effectively losing over a dollar for every dollar earned.
In the first six months of 2019, WeWork reported an operating loss of $1.37 billion and a net loss attributable to WeWork of $904.7 million on revenue of $1.54 billion.
WeWork introduced an invented non-GAAP metric called 'Community Adjusted EBITDA' which stripped out normal operating expenses including building lease payments (rent).
As of June 30, 2019, WeWork had committed to $47.2 billion in future lease payments to commercial landlords, while its customer commitments totaled only approximately $4 billion.
In 2019, The We Company paid $5.9 million in stock to WE Holdings LLC (controlled by Adam Neumann and founders) to acquire the trademark for the word 'We'.
Adam Neumann owned stakes in several commercial properties that were leased back to WeWork, earning him millions in rental income from his own company.

The initial S-1 gave Adam Neumann Class B and C shares with 20 votes per share, and named his wife Rebekah Neumann to a 3-person committee with sole power to name a successor CEO upon his death or disability.
WeWork purchased a luxury Gulfstream G650 private jet for approximately $60 million in 2018 for corporate travel.
WeWork arranged a $6 billion debt facility with JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs that was explicitly contingent on raising at least $3 billion in the equity IPO.
Following severe institutional investor backlash to the S-1, WeWork withdrew its IPO on September 17, 2019, and Adam Neumann resigned as CEO on September 24, 2019.

Facing a projected cash exhaustion date by November 2019, WeWork accepted a SoftBank takeover valuing the equity at roughly $8 billion, while Neumann secured a multi-hundred-million-dollar exit package.
In February 2021, SoftBank settled litigation in the Delaware Court of Chancery with Neumann and WeWork, resulting in Neumann cashing out approximately $480 million in stock.
On November 6, 2023, WeWork filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey with over $18 billion in debt, completely wiping out original shareholders before emerging in May 2024.
In 2017, SoftBank founder Masayoshi Son took a 12-minute tour of WeWork and asked Adam Neumann whether the smart guy or crazy guy wins in a fight, telling him he was 'not crazy enough'.
